definition: An inference acceleration technique where an auxiliary draft model generates candidate tokens validated in parallel by a larger target model.
details: Speculative decoding converts autoregressive generation from memory-bandwidth-bound steps into compute-bound parallel operations by checking multiple tokens simultaneously with target model logits, maintaining exact probability distributions.

explainer.lead: An inference acceleration technique in which a small draft model proposes candidate tokens that a larger target model validates in parallel. It matters because it speeds generation while keeping exact output probabilities.

tiers.eli5: A fast helper scribbles several guesses ahead, and the expert checks them all at once instead of writing every word alone.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pair a cheap draft model with the target model and verify several proposed tokens per target pass. A pitfall is that any gain depends on draft acceptance, so a poorly matched draft model wastes effort.
tiers.paperLevel: Candidate tokens from an auxiliary draft model are validated in parallel using target model logits, converting memory-bandwidth-bound autoregressive steps into compute-bound parallel operations while maintaining exact probability distributions.

explainer.example: A small draft model proposes five tokens, the target model checks them in one forward pass, and the accepted prefix is kept while the rest is resampled.

citation.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
